sanskrit: devī devyāṃ jātāsi pṛthivyām adhy oṣadhe | tāṃ tvā nitatni keśebhyo dṛṃhaṇāya khanāmasi ||
english: O divine herb, you were born of the divine one, upon the earth; we dig you up, with your roots spread wide, for the strengthening of [the] hair.

sanskrit: indras tvākhanat prathamo varuṇasya duhitṛbhyaḥ | dṛṃha jātāñ janayājātān ye jātās tān u varṣīyasas kṛdhi ||
english: Indra dug you up first, from among the daughters of Varuṇa. Strengthen those already born, bring forth the unborn, and those that have been born—make them yet more vigorous.

sanskrit: yas te keśo 'vatataḥ samūlo yaś ca vṛhyate | sarvaṃ taṃ viśvabheṣajyā- -abhi ṣiñcāmi vīrudhā ||
english: Whatever hair of yours has fallen down together with its root, and whatever is being torn out—all of that I sprinkle with this plant of universal healing power.

sanskrit: abhīśunā meyo 'stu viyāmenānumeyaḥ | keśo naḍa iva vardhatāṃ śīrṣṇas te asitas pari ||
english: Let it be immeasurable by the near measure, to be estimated only by the far measure; may the hair grow like a reed all around the crown of your head, dark and thick.

sanskrit: yathā naḍaṃ kaśipune striyo bhindanty aśmanā | evā bhinadmi te muṣkau tasmai tvām avase huve ||
english: As women crush a reed in a mortar with a stone, so do I crush your testicles; for that purpose I invoke you for aid.

sanskrit: tvaṃ vīrudhāṃ śreṣṭhatamā- -abhiśrutāsy oṣadhe | sāmum adya pūruṣaṃ klībam opaśinaṃ kṛdhi ||
english: You are the most excellent among plants, O herb, renowned and celebrated; make this man today a eunuch, impotent and devoid of sexual power.

sanskrit: klībaṃ kṛdhy opaśinam atho kurīriṇaṃ kṛdhi | ubhābhyām asya grāvabhyām indro bhinattv āṇḍyau ||
english: Make him a eunuch, bereft of virility; further, make him one who wears the kurīra [woman's headgear as a mark of emasculation]; may Indra cleave asunder both his testicles with both pressing-stones.

sanskrit: klība klībaṃ tvākaraṃ vadhre vadhriṃ tvākaram | arasārasaṃ tvākaram arasāraso 'si | kurīram asya śīrṣaṇi kumbaṃ cādhi ni dadhmasi ||
english: O eunuch, I have made you a eunuch; O castrate, I have made you a castrate; I have made you utterly devoid of semen—you are semen-drained. We place both the kurīra and the kumba [woman's coiffure-ornaments] upon his head.

sanskrit: ye te nāḍyau devakṛte yayos tiṣṭhati vṛṣṇyam | te te bhinadmi śamyayā- -amuṣyā adhi muṣkayoḥ ||
english: Those two veins of yours, made by the gods, in which the virile essence resides—those two I split asunder with a pin, upon that one's testicles.

sanskrit: jāyamāno nir arujat sapatnān dodhato 'bhayān | sa vai sapatnānāṃ sabhā avālapsyo anāśayat ||
english: Being born he broke asunder his rivals, those who were bold and fearless; he it is who, as the avālapsya [amulet], destroyed the assembly of rivals.

sanskrit: ārād arātiṃ kṛṇute aśastim apa bādhate | avālapsyaḥ sa yo maṇiḥ sahasvān abhimātihā ||
english: He puts the foe at a distance and thrusts away ill-fortune; that amulet is avālapsya, mighty, the slayer of enemies.

sanskrit: cakṣur asya sūtram āsīt tardma śrotram utābharat | avālapsyaḥ sa yo maṇiḥ sahasvān abhimātihā ||
english: His eye was the thread [of creation], his ear bore the awl; that amulet is avālapsya, mighty, the slayer of enemies.

sanskrit: imaṃ maṇim āvālapsyaṃ yasminn ārohayāmasi | sa vai sapatnān ā datte sa enaṃ pātu viśvataḥ sa enaṃ jarase nayāt ||
english: This āvālapsya amulet upon which we cause [the wearer] to mount—he indeed takes possession of rivals; may it protect him from all sides; may it lead him to old age.
